turns.match: highlight the three main claims and comment on the weakest
turns.script:
scene layout=page
say x1 title | Paine, Common Sense: three claims
say x2 strong | 1. Society and government are different things, with different origins.
say x3 aside | Society is produced by our wants, and government by our wickedness.
say x4 strong | 2. Society is always a blessing; government is at best a necessary evil.
say x5 aside | At worst it is intolerable, because we pay for the thing that harms us.
say x6 strong | 3. Government exists only because conscience fails.
say x7 aside | Were the impulses of conscience clear, uniform, and irresistibly obeyed, man would need no other lawgiver.
wait 1
say x8 title | The weakest: claim 1
say x9 | Paine says government comes from wickedness alone. That does not hold up. Much of what governments do has nothing to do with vice. Roads, weights and measures, which side of the road to drive on, and defence against outsiders are problems of coordination. A society of saints would still need them.
say x10 | So government also grows out of our *wants*, the same root Paine gives society. The clean line between the two blurs. Claim 3 inherits the flaw: perfect conscience tells you to be good, but it does not tell everyone which shared rule to follow.
say x11 | Claim 2 is a value judgement, but it follows from claim 1. Weaken claim 1 and "necessary evil" starts to look more like "necessary tool".
say x12 aside | Paine's point was rhetorical, not careful theory. In January 1776 he needed government to look like a burden the colonies could reshape.
say x13 choice | Steelman Paine's reply
say x14 choice | Compare with Hobbes and Locke

scene layout=page
say x15 strong | Paine's "necessary evil" rests on where government comes from.
say x16 | Claim 2 isn't a fact you can check. It's a verdict: government is bad, even if we can't do without it.
say x17 | That verdict comes from claim 1. If government is born only from our wickedness, it is a mark of our faults. We put up with it, like a lock on a door.
say x18 | But if government also grows out of our *needs*, like roads, shared measures and agreeing which side of the road to drive on, it's no longer just a sign of failure. It's something we build to get things done together.
say x19 | Then "necessary evil" turns into "necessary tool": still needed, but no longer bad in itself.
say x20 aside | In short: knock out the origin story and the moral verdict loses its footing.
say x21 choice | Steelman Paine's reply
say x22 choice | Compare with Hobbes and Locke
